result.markdown: --- title: "Session 2 — Discrimination and Calibration" subtitle: "ROC and AUC · thresholds · sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV · calibration plot, slope and intercept · Brier score · Lab 2" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Session 1: a model that gives a **risk** for each adult - Today: **how good** are these risks? Two questions: - **Discrimination**: does the model **rank** adults with diabetes above those without? - **Calibration**: are the **risks themselves right**? - (Both are still **apparent** here: in the development data) ::: # Topic 1 — Discrimination {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## ROC curve and AUC ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} roc1 <- roc(dev$diabetes, dev$risk, quiet = TRUE) plot(roc1, legacy.axes = TRUE, col = col_blue, lwd = 3, print.auc = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s2_discrimination_calibration_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ci.auc(roc1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 95% CI: 0.745-0.847 (DeLong) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} **AUC 0.80** (95% CI 0.75 to 0.85). It is the probability that a **randomly chosen adult with diabetes has a higher predicted risk** than one without. **0.5 = coin toss, 1 = perfect**. A common reading: 0.7 to 0.8 acceptable, 0.8 to 0.9 good, but the **usefulness depends on the use**. ::: ## A threshold ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tab <- table(predicted = dev$risk >= 0.15, diabetes = dev$diabetes); tab ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` diabetes predicted 0 1 FALSE 483 32 TRUE 133 52 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} round(c(sensitivity = tab["TRUE", "1"] / sum(tab[, "1"]), specificity = tab["FALSE", "0"] / sum(tab[, "0"]), PPV = tab["TRUE", "1"] / sum(tab["TRUE", ]), NPV = tab["FALSE", "0"] / sum(tab["FALSE", ])), 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` sensitivity specificity PPV NPV 0.62 0.78 0.28 0.94 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - At **15%**: sensitivity **0.62**, specificity **0.78**, PPV **0.28**, NPV **0.94** - **Lower the threshold**: sensitivity **up**, specificity **down** (more adults tested) - **PPV and NPV depend on the prevalence**: they change from district to district - The **AUC** summarises **all thresholds**; the **choice of threshold** needs **costs and benefits** (Session 5) ::: ## Added value ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} c(age_only = auc_of(dev$diabetes, predict(glm(diabetes ~ age, data = dev, family = binomial), type = "response")), full_model = auc_of(dev$diabetes, dev$risk)) |> round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` age_only full_model 0.682 0.796 ``` ::: ::: Age alone gives **0.68**; the full model **0.80**: the other predictors add **real discrimination**. # Topic 2 — Calibration {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Calibration plot ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} cal <- dev |> mutate(decile = ntile(risk, 10)) |> group_by(decile) |> summarise(predicted = mean(risk), observed = mean(diabetes)) ggplot(cal, aes(predicted, observed)) + geom_abline(linetype = 2) + geom_point(size = 3, colour = col_blue) + geom_line(colour = col_blue) + coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 0.6), ylim = c(0, 0.6)) + labs(x = "Mean predicted risk", y = "Observed proportion with diabetes") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s2_discrimination_calibration_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.key} Group the adults by **deciles of predicted risk** and compare the **mean predicted** with the **observed** proportion. **Points on the diagonal** = well calibrated. **Below** = the model **over-estimates**; **above** = it **under-estimates**. ::: ## Calibration slope and intercept ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} lp <- qlogis(dev$risk) round(coef(glm(diabetes ~ lp, data = dev, family = binomial)), 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` (Intercept) lp 0 1 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.warn} Intercept **0** and slope **1.000** in the development data: this is **guaranteed** when a logistic model is fitted by maximum likelihood. It says **nothing** about new patients. In **new data**: **slope below 1** = predictions **too extreme** (overfitting); **intercept (calibration-in-the-large)** shows **average over- or under-estimation**. ::: ## Brier score ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} brier <- mean((dev$risk - dev$diabetes)^2); brier_null <- mean((mean(dev$diabetes) - dev$diabetes)^2) round(c(brier = brier, scaled = 1 - brier / brier_null), 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` brier scaled 0.089 0.155 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **Brier** = mean squared difference between **risk and outcome** (0 = perfect); combines **discrimination and calibration** - **Scaled Brier** = 1 − Brier / Brier of "everyone gets the prevalence": **0.15** here (0 = no better than the prevalence) - Avoid the **Hosmer-Lemeshow test**: it depends on the grouping, has low power and says **nothing about how** the calibration fails ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 2 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `prediction-workshop/labs/lab2_perf.R` - ROC, AUC and its CI - threshold, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV - calibration plot, slope, Brier score ::: **Time:** 40 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="p2q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="iowk9i.7wdo2c" data-show="QSByYW5kb20gY2FzZSBoYXMgYSBoaWdoZXIgcmlzayB0aGFuIGEgcmFuZG9tIG5vbi1jYXNl LCA4MCUgb2YgdGhlIHRpbWU=" data-explain="VGhlIEFVQyBpcyB0aGUgcHJvYmFiaWxpdHkgdGhhdCBhIHJhbmRvbWx5IGNob3NlbiBjYXNl IGhhcyBhIGhpZ2hlciBwcmVkaWN0ZWQgcmlzayB0aGFuIGEgcmFuZG9tbHkgY2hvc2VuIG5v bi1jYXNlLiBJdCBzYXlzIG5vdGhpbmcgYWJvdXQgdGhlIGNhbGlicmF0aW9uIG9mIHRoZSBy aXNrcy4="} How do you read an AUC of 0.80? - 80% of the adults are classified correctly if a threshold of 50% is used - The predicted risks are within 20% of the true risks, on average, for adults - A random case has a higher risk than a random non-case, 80% of the time - The model explains 80% of the variation in diabetes within the cohort studied ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="p2q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="iowxi6.7we2jo" data-show="U2Vuc2l0aXZpdHkgcmlzZXMgYW5kIHNwZWNpZmljaXR5IGZhbGxz" data-explain="QSBsb3dlciB0aHJlc2hvbGQgbGFiZWxzIG1vcmUgYWR1bHRzIGFzIHBvc2l0aXZlLCBzbyBt b3JlIGNhc2VzIGFyZSBmb3VuZCAoaGlnaGVyIHNlbnNpdGl2aXR5KSBidXQgbW9yZSBub24t Y2FzZXMgYXJlIGxhYmVsbGVkIHBvc2l0aXZlIChsb3dlciBzcGVjaWZpY2l0eSku"} A threshold of 15% gives a sensitivity of 0.62. What happens when the threshold is lowered to 5%? - Both sensitivity and specificity rise - Sensitivity rises and specificity falls - Sensitivity falls and specificity rises - Neither changes, since the AUC does not depend on the threshold ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="p2q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="ioxaqw.7weh12" data-show="Tm90aGluZyBhYm91dCBuZXcgcGF0aWVudHM6IGl0IGlzIGd1YXJhbnRlZWQgYnkgdGhlIGZp dHRpbmc=" data-explain="TWF4aW11bSBsaWtlbGlob29kIGZvcmNlcyB0aGUgYXBwYXJlbnQgY2FsaWJyYXRpb24gdG8g YmUgcGVyZmVjdC4gQ2FsaWJyYXRpb24gaGFzIHRvIGJlIGFzc2Vzc2VkIGluIG5ldyBkYXRh IG9yIHdpdGggYSBib290c3RyYXAu"} In the development data the calibration slope is exactly 1 and the intercept 0. What does this tell you? - The model is well calibrated and will be well calibrated in other cohorts - The model does not overfit, since the slope is not below 1 in these data - Nothing about new patients: it is guaranteed by the fitting - The predicted risks are accurate for each of the risk groups in the cohort ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="p2q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="ioxnzm.7wevig" data-show="VGhlIG1vZGVsIG92ZXItZXN0aW1hdGVzIHJpc2s6IGZld2VyIGV2ZW50cyBhcmUgb2JzZXJ2 ZWQgdGhhbiBwcmVkaWN0ZWQ=" data-explain="T2JzZXJ2ZWQgcHJvcG9ydGlvbnMgYmVsb3cgcHJlZGljdGVkIG9uZXMgbWVhbiB0aGF0IHRo ZSBwcmVkaWN0ZWQgcmlzayBpcyB0b28gaGlnaC4gRGlzY3JpbWluYXRpb24gaXMgYSBzZXBh cmF0ZSBxdWVzdGlvbi4="} In a calibration plot the points lie below the diagonal at high predicted risk. What does that mean? - The model under-estimates risk, since more events are observed than predicted - The model discriminates poorly, with an AUC close to 0.5 - The sample is too small to draw a calibration plot - The model over-estimates risk: fewer events are observed than predicted ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="p2q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="ioy188.7wf9zq" data-show="VGhleSBkZXBlbmQgb24gdGhlIHByZXZhbGVuY2Ugb2YgdGhlIGRpc2Vhc2UgaW4gdGhlIHBv cHVsYXRpb24=" data-explain="UHJlZGljdGl2ZSB2YWx1ZXMgY29tYmluZSBzZW5zaXRpdml0eSBhbmQgc3BlY2lmaWNpdHkg d2l0aCB0aGUgcHJldmFsZW5jZS4gV2l0aCBhIGhpZ2hlciBwcmV2YWxlbmNlLCB0aGUgUFBW IHJpc2VzIGFuZCB0aGUgTlBWIGZhbGxzLg=="} Why do PPV and NPV differ between a screening clinic and the general population for the same model? - They depend on the prevalence of the disease in the population - The AUC of the model changes with the setting by definition - Sensitivity and specificity are defined in clinics but not elsewhere - The threshold has to be changed when the setting changes ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **Discrimination**: AUC = chance of ranking a case above a non-case - **Threshold**: sensitivity, specificity; PPV/NPV depend on **prevalence** - **Calibration**: plot, **slope** (spread), **intercept** (average level) - Apparent slope is always **1**: check in **new data** - **Brier** combines both; avoid Hosmer-Lemeshow ::: **Next:** Session 3: overfitting and internal validation

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
